edges.notes: Linux documents and maintains a RISC-V architecture port.
LLVM targets RISC-V in mainstream backends.
RISC-V ELF psABI and ELF flags are part of the platform ABI story alongside the ISA manuals.
GNU as/ld include RISC-V targets for assembly and linking.
LLVM/lld supports RISC-V among LLVM targets.
GCC includes a RISC-V backend alongside GNU binutils targets.
glibc supports GNU/Linux on RISC-V alongside the ELF psABI and ISA manuals.
musl includes Linux support on RISC-V among its documented architecture ports.
GCC provides libstdc++ for supported RISC-V GNU/Linux targets alongside the C library.
LLVM/Clang libc++ is available for RISC-V targets in LLVM cross and native toolchains.
LLVM ships libc++abi for RISC-V alongside libc++ in LLVM toolchains.
RISC-V embedded GCC distributions commonly include newlib for bare-metal and small-hosted targets.
